cells.tense: Care is moving through you right now, and it is not straining to hold anything in place.
cells.act: surrender the outcome and keep the act
cells.ask: Keep watering what you're growing and stop watching how it lands. Do the work each day; skip the checking.
cells.core:
Something near you is getting the real thing — attention that lets it come along at its own speed. You're not standing over it. You water it and step back, and because you step back, you can tell what's growing from what you're propping up by hand. That's why none of it feels like hauling.

What's here to do next is small. Choose whichever one you're tending, keep tending it, and stop managing where it lands. Drop the outcome, stay with the work, and you'll see it holds without you hovering. Watch the pull to grip harder as it nears something. Let finishing do the letting-go.
cells.sheetLine: Care that doesn't clutch is what lets it grow.
cells.verb: tending what is developing and letting it come up without forcing it
cells.place: the ground before anything has chosen what it will be yet

cells.tense: You are already arranging how this will go, and it has not started yet.
cells.act: let the path show itself instead of forcing clarity
cells.ask: When you catch yourself planning how it should go, stop and take the step plainly there. No timetable.
cells.core:
Done well, this looks like standing close enough to tend and far enough back that the thing grows toward its own light — care arriving on time and at the size of what's there. Instead you're seeing the whole finished shape in advance and getting out ahead of it: more structure, more protection, more you. It starts reaching for your light instead of its own.

You don't need the whole road, only the next stretch. Let that show itself. Sketch what's already there, badly, and keep the sketch rather than redrawing it. Then take one step and stay in the murk. "I'll see how it goes" is a sentence you can stand in.
cells.sheetLine: You're ahead of it, holding a shape it hasn't chosen yet.

cells.tense: Nothing has come up here for a long while, and you have been standing beside it the whole time.
cells.act: move toward the thing you actually want
cells.ask: Turn toward what you'd hate most to lose and take a step you can see from here. No particular time.
cells.core:
You've kept yourself clear of it. From outside that reads as unbothered, fine on your own, and it holds up as long as nobody asks. Nothing has started growing either, and standing back from everything looks the same as not needing anything. What it looks like when it's well: you're aimed at something and moving toward it in small visible steps, and the aim is what lets the rest come up around you.

Find what you'd hate most to lose and face it plainly, to yourself first. A step you can actually see. You don't have to want it with feeling. Just go where the light is.

cells.tense: Somewhere along the way you became the one holding this up, and you did not decide that.
cells.act: put it down and leave your hands empty a while
cells.ask: Set down something you're carrying for someone else, without saying so, and don't reach for it again that day.
cells.core:
People bring you what needs tending, and mostly you tend it. You'd say you're just the reliable one. That reliability isn't a trait that happened to you — it's work, it's yours, and it keeps going whether or not you agreed to it this round. That's why it's tiring in a way rest doesn't touch.

Letting go is yours to do, a piece at a time. Take something you're carrying for someone and set it down quietly. Then let your hands stay open for a day. The open hands are the point — they're how you find the line between what you chose and what came at you.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding things up that you didn't agree to carry.

A reader could reasonably say the block is about skill or time, not about holding something shut, and the ask still works if that's true because it only moves a body toward one thing without requiring a feeling. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line implying I know what they're holding — I've kept the asks doing the work and left the reasons unknown.
